questions.question: In which state of India is Nishagandhi festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Kerala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Nishagandhi festival** is observed** twice a year,** once in the months of **October and November **and again in **March and April.**
 
• It takes place in the **Nishagandhi Theatre** within the grounds of **Kanakunnu Palace** in** Trivandrum, Kerala.**
 
• This festival lasts for roughly a week and** attracts artisans** from all around the nation.
 
• The Nishagandhi Dance Festival's artists who are committed to highlighting th**e rich diversity of Indian traditions **are an essential component.
 
• The **Kerala Tourist Development Corporation** organizes the Nishagandhi Dance Festival.
 
• Other states occasionally **co-host **it as well.
 
• Recently, this celebration was co-hosted by **West Bengal and Rajasthan.**
 
• Other** famous festivals** of Kerala are - Onam,

 Attukal Pongala, Vishu, Thrissur Pooram, Theyyam Festival, Boat Race Festival, Makaravilakku, Adoor Gajamela.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Ratha Jatra, Magha Saptami, Makara Mela, Chhau festival, Puri Beach festival, Naukhai, Chatar Jatra, Durga Puja, Kalinga Mahatsav, Chandan Yatra, Konark Dance Festival, Mahabisuva Sankranti.
 
 

 Madhya Pradesh

questions.question: The famous song 'Aye Mere Watan Ke Logo' was originally sung by _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lata Mangeshkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aye Mere Watan Ke Logo 

 
 
• It is a patriotic song written in Hindi by Kavi Pradeep, composed by C. Ramchandra, and sung by singer Lata Mangeshkar. Hence, Option 2 is correct.
 
• The song commemorates Indian soldiers who died during the Sino-Indian War in 1962.
 
• The song was first performed live two months after the war by Mangeshkar on Republic Day (26 January) 1963 at the National Stadium in New Delhi in the presence of President Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kavi Pradeep

 
 
• He was born Ramchandra Narayanji Dwivedi.
 
• He was an Indian poet and songwriter who is best known for his patriotic song Aye Mere Watan Ke Logo written as a tribute to the soldiers who had died defending the country during the Sino-Indian War.

questions.question: Who among the following took the title of ‘Ghazi’ after defeating Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Babur.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur of the Mughal Empire** and** Rajput King Rana Sanga of Mewar** fought each other in** Khanwa, 60 kilometers west of Agra.**
 
• The event to gain control of** Northern India **took place on **March 16, 1527. **
 
• **Sangram Singh** was regarded as one of** India's greatest historical figures.**
 
• Rana Sanga aspired to be the** supreme leader** of India.
 
• The** Khanwa battle **was won by **Babur.**
 
• After the** Battle of Khanwa,** Babur held the title of **Ghazi (17th March 1527).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Daulat Khan Lodhi:**

 
 
• During **Ibrahim Lodi's reign **as the Lodi dynasty's last king, he served as the** city's governor.**
 
• **Around 1500–1525,** Daulat Khan Lodhi served as **governor of Punjab, **having been chosen by the Lodhi Sultan of the time.
 
 
 
• **Humayun:**
 
 
• The **Mughal Empire's second emperor** was named Humayun.
 
• After being beaten by an **Afghan soldier** named **Sher Shah of Sur **in **1539 in Chausa **and in **1540 at Kannauj, **Humayun was banished from India.
 
 
 
• **Mahmud Shah I:**
 
 
• The** Gujarat Sultanate's** most notable Ruler was **Mahmud Shah I.**
 
• He was in charge of bringing down the **Dwarkadhish Temple in Gujarat's Dwarka. **

questions.question: Mona writes about an ocean that separates North America from Europe. Which ocean is it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atlantic Ocean**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Atlantic Ocean is located between North and South America and also between Europe and Africa.**

 
 
• It is the second-largest ocean and has a depth of about 12000 ft.
 
 
 
• **It separates Africa from South America and North America from Europe. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• **Mediterranean Sea, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, Hudson Bay, Labrador Sea etc are some of the biggest seas in the Atlantic Ocean.**
 
• Europe comprises of peninsula of Eurasia in the Northern Hemisphere and shares its landmass with both Asia and Africa.
 
 
• **The Ural mountains separate Europe from Asia. **
 
 
 
• North America lies in the Northern Hemisphere and completely in the Western Hemisphere bordered by the Arctic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest Ocean in the world and is the coldest ocean of all. **

 
 
• It is surrounded by Eurasia and North America and also Bering Strait.
 
 
 
• **The Indian Ocean is the world's third-largest ocean** surrounded by Asia, Africa and Australia.
 
 
• Many major seas like the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Andaman Sea drain into the Indan Ocean.
 
 
 
• **The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world** which extends from the Arctic Ocean to Antarctica.
 
 
• **The deepest location on Earth, the Mariana Trench is located in the Pacific Ocean.**

questions.question: What is the term of State Legislative Assembly in India as per Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• State Legislative Assemblies are analogous to Lok Sabha.
 
• The term is of State Legislative Assemblies is Five Year.
 
 
• Each Legislative Assemblies in India is formed for a period of five years, after which all seats are up for election.
 
 
 
• A person must not be less than 25 years of age to become a member of State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• Money bills can be introduced in the state legislative assembly only with the prior recommendation of the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• State Legislative Assemblies are also known as Vidhan Sabhas.
 
• State Legislative Assembly is chaired by the speaker.
 
• The Governor can summon and prorogue the state legislation and dissolve the state legislative assembly.
 
• State Legislative Assembly is directly elected by the people.
 
 
• Each Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is directly elected to serve 5-year terms by single-member constituencies.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was called ‘Amitrochates’ by the Greeks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara **was the **second Mauryan emperor** of India and the son of** Chandragupta Maurya,** the **founder of the Maurya dynasty.**
 
• The Greeks gave him the illustrious name** Amitraghata (or Amitrochates)**, which translates to "**the destroyer of enemies" **in Sanskrit.
 
• The **Sanskrit word** "Amitraghata" is a combination of the two words** "Amitra" and "Ghata".**
 
• According to a Sanskrit dictionary, "**Amrita**" denotes an **adversary or antagonist,** while **"Ghata"** denotes **destruction or murder.**
 
• He was left with a vast empire by Chandragupta Maurya that comprised **Baluchistan, Afghanistan, Assam, Orissa, West Bengal, Bihar, Mysore, Vindhyas, Narmada, and Hindukush.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta:**

 
 
• The **second ruler** of the ancient Indian **Gupta Empire **was Samudragupta.
 
• Samudragupta earned the nickname **"Napoleon of India"** for the conflicts he fought.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta I:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, which ruled over parts of **northern and central India,** was headed by Chandragupta I.
 
 
 
• **Kaniska:**
 
 
• **Kanishka I** was an emperor of the** Kushan dynasty**, under whose rule the kingdom attained its height.
 
• His title **Maharajadhiraja** denotes that he was the first ruler of the dynasty.
 
• The **fourth major Buddhist council,** which launched **Mahayana Buddhism**, was called in **Kashmir by Kaniska,** who is most famous for that.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles under Directive Principles of State Policy, in the Indian constitution provides the organisation of village panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 40.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 40,** 

 
 
• The State shall take steps to **organise village panchayats **and 
 
• endow them with such** powers and authority** as may be necessary to enable them to function as **units of self-government.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Article 60:**

 
 
• In accordance with **Article 60** of the Indian Constitution, the **President **must take an **oath or affirmation.**
 
• It stipulates that the** Chief Justice of India**, or, in his absence, the **senior-most Supreme Court judge** available, administers the oath of office to the President.
 
• The same oath or affirmation is taken by any other **individual **serving as president or carrying out the **president's duties.**
 
 
 
• **Article 50:**
 
 
• The State shall take steps to **separate the judiciary from the executive **in the public services of the State.
 
 
 
• **Article 30:**
 
 
• Article 30 of the Indian Constitution states the **right of minorities** to establish and administer **educational institutions. **

questions.question: According to the data from the economic think-tank, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE), which of the following states witnessed the highest unemployment rate as of January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy, **an economic research tank, reported that** Haryana** has the** highest unemployment rate** in January 2022 at **23.4%.**
 
• It was followed by **Jammu & Kashmir** (15%),** Rajasthan** (18.9%),** Tripura** (17.1%), and** Delh**i (14.1%).
 
• With a **0.7% unemployment** rate in January, **Telangana** had the** lowest rate.**
 
• **Gujarat** came in second at** 1.2%**, followed by **Meghalaya** at **1.5, Odisha** at **1.8%**, and **Karnataka at 2.9%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CMIE data** show that **India's unemployment rate** in January 2022 dramatically **decreased to 6.57%.**
 
• The rate hasn't been this low since **March 2021.**
 
• The unemployment rate increased from **6.97% in November** to a four-month high of **7.91% in December 2021.**
 
• According to area-specific data, rural unemployment fell from **7.28% in December 2021 **to **5.84% in January 2022.**
 
• **8.16% **of** urban residents** were unemployed, down from **9.30% in December 2021.**

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Choose the most reactive metal from the options given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **chemical element sodium** has the **atomic number 11** and the **symbol Na.**
 
• It is a **delicate, silvery-white metal** that is exceedingly reactive.
 
• Due to its placement in **group 1 of the periodic table,** sodium is an** alkali metal.**
 
• Due to its** extremely reactive nature**, it is not found as a **pure metal** in nature.
 
• Because sodium is so** intensely reactive, **even simply water alone can set off **explosions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper:**

 
 
• On a scale of reactivity, **copper is low.**
 
• Its** malleability and low reactivity** make it perfect for usage in architecture.
 
• Copper may be** carved and hammered** into intricate forms.
 
• It will shield itself with a** patina, a light-green layer of copper salts.**
 
 
 
• **Zinc:**
 
 
• With **acids, alkalis, and other non-metals**, zinc interacts easily.
 
• At normal temperatures, extremely **pure zinc only moderately interacts **with acids.
 
 
 
• **Iron:**
 
 
• A particularly **active metal is iron.**
 
• In humid air, it easily **mixes with oxygen.**
 
• **Rust** is made of iron oxide, a byproduct of this process.
 
• **Hydrogen gas is** also created when iron combines with extremely hot water and steam.​

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Mughal architecture under Aurangzeb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Moti Masjid, Delhi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Inside the** Red Fort complex **in Delhi, India is a** mosque** made of white marble called **Moti Masjid.**
 
• It is situated next to the **Diwan-i-Khas **and to the west of the** Hammam.**
 
• **Aurangzeb, the Mughal emperor,** constructed it between **1659 and 1660.**
 
• It cost **Rs.160,000 **to build the mosque.
 
• The prayer hall is separated into **two aisles** and has **three arches.**
 
• **Three bulbous domes** that were originally **made of gilded copper **adorn its top.
 
• The **1857 Indian uprising** led to the loss of the **gilded copper.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahal, Agra:**

 
 
• **An Islamic ivory-white marble monument** known as the Taj Mahal is located in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India**, on the right bank of the** Yamuna River.**
 
• **Shah Jahan**, the fifth Mughal emperor, commissioned it in **1631.**
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid, Delhi:**
 
 
• One of the **biggest mosques **in India is called Jama Masjid.
 
• **Shah Jahan, **the Mughal monarch, constructed it between **1650 and 1656.**
 
• **Syed Abdul Ghafoor Shah Bukhari,** the first Imam, performed the inauguration.
 
 
 
• **Qutab Minar, Delhi:**
 
 
• **A "victory tower"** and minaret, Qutab Minar is a component of the Qutb complex.
 
• On the remains of the **Lal Kot, the Dhillika citadel **was constructed by the Qutb Minar.
 
• After the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, which was begun in **1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak,** the first sultan of Delhi, Qutub Minar was built.

questions.question: Which of the following was set up in 1956 by the Indian government by nationalising all the existing private sector life insurance companies?

__
 
• **Life Insurance Company is a public sector insurance company headquartered in Mumbai that was incorporated by Insurance Act in June 1956.**

questions.question: India and Sri Lanka are joined by a group of islets forming ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adam's Bridge.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adam's bridge or Ram Setu bridge is located between Rameshwaram Island (or Pamban Island) in Tamil Nadu and Mannar Island, Sri Lanka. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
• The bridge is around 50 km long and is made up of a chain of limestones, and coral reefs.
 
 
• **It separates Palk Strait in the northeast and the Gulf of Mannar in the southwest. **
 
 
 
• It starts at Dhanushkodi in Pamban Island and follows through Mannar Island where it is connected to the Sri Lanka land.
 
• Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project (SSCP) was inaugurated in 2005 and is a channel that connects Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhupen Hazarika Bridge or referred to as the Dhola-Sadiya bridge connects the northeastern states of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh and is built across the Lohit River, which is a tributary of the Brahmaputra river.**

 
 
• With its length of around 9.15 km, it is the longest bridge in India over water.
 
 
 
• **Sisseri River bridge, a 200-meter long bridge connecting Dibang Valley and Siang in Arunachal Pradesh** inaugurated by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in 2019.
 
 
• The bridge was constructed by Project Brahmank of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).
 
• **Sisseri River is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River.**

questions.question: Which of the following was a revolutionary organisation formed outside India in 1913?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ghadar Party__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ghadar party was an international political movement organized by Indians to end British rule in India.
 
 
• It was formed in 1913.
 
• Headquarters was at Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco, United States of America.
 
• It was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Hardayal.
 
• The Ghadar Party was organized by migrant Indians in the United States.
 
• The old name of the Ghadar Party was the Pacific coast Hindustan association.
 
• The name Ghadar party was adopted after the launch of its journal Ghadar in 1913.
 
• It was formally dissolved in 1948.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Bharatiya Janata Party was founded on April 6, 1980, and is headquartered in Delhi.

 
 
• It is based on the ideology of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission: **
 
 
• The British government appointed the Simon Commission to review the Government of India Act 1919 in the year 1927.
 
• The Simon commission arrived in India in 1928.__
 
• It was formed to study constitutional reforms and make recommendations to the government in India.
 
• Simon commission was an all-white commission without any Indian members.
 
• The commission consisted of seven Englishman and sir John Simon was its chairman.
 
• It was formed on 26th November 1927.
 
• Simon commission arrived in India on __3rd February 1928.__
 
• The Madras session of the congress passed a resolution to boycott the Simon Commission.
 
• Simon commission submitted its reports on 27th May 1930.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress:**

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Which of the following socio religious communities was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Brahmo Samaj:-

 
• Brahmo Samaj is the societal component of Brahmoism, which began as a monotheistic reformist movement of the Hindu religion that appeared during the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• It was one of the most influential religious movements in India and made a significant contribution to the making of modern India.
 
• It was started at Calcutta on 20 August 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore as the reformation of the prevailing Brahmanism of the time (specifically Kulin practices) and began the Bengal Renaissance of the 19th century pioneering all religious, social, and educational advancement of the Hindu community in the 19th century.
 
• Its Trust Deed was made in 1830 formalizing its inception and it was duly and publicly inaugurated in January 1830 by the consecration of the first house of prayer, now known as the Adi Brahmo Samaj.
 
• From the Brahmo Samaj springs Brahmoism, the most recent of legally recognized religions in India and Bangladesh, reflecting its foundation on reformed spiritual Hinduism with vital elements of Judeo-Islamic faith and practice.

 Raja Ram Mohan Roy

 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the father of Modern India’s Renaissance and a tireless social reformer who inaugurated the age of enlightenment and liberal reformist modernization in India.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born on 22nd May 1772 in Bengal.
 
• His early education included the study of Persian and Arabic at Patna where he read the Quran, the works of Sufi mystic poets, and the Arabic translation of the works of Plato and Aristotle.
 
• In Benaras, he studied Sanskrit and read Vedas and Upnishads.
 
• From 1803 to 1814, he worked for East India Company as the personal diwan first of Woodforde and then of Digby.
 
• In 1814, he resigned from his job and moved to Calcutta in order to devote his life to religious, social, and political reforms.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s first published work Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhiddin (a gift to deists) published in 1803 exposed irrational religious beliefs and corrupt practices of the Hindus as the belief in revelations, prophets, miracles, etc.
 
• He founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814, the Calcutta Unitarian Association in 1821, and the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 which later became the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He campaigned against the caste system, untouchability, superstitions, and the use of intoxicants.
 
• He was well known for his pioneering thought and action on the emancipation of women and especially on the abolition of Sati and widow remarriage.
 
• Roy did much to disseminate the benefits of modern education to his countrymen.
 
• He supported David Hare’s efforts to find the Hindu College in 1817, while Roy’s English school taught mechanics and Voltaire’s philosophy.
 
• In 1825, he established Vedanta college where courses in both Indian learning and Western social and physical sciences were offered.

questions.question: Which natural compound helps in photosynthesis of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Chlorophyll__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chlorophyll:

 
 
• It is a green-coloured pigment that is found in plants and helps in photosynthesis.
 
• The structure of chlorophyll is similar to that of haemoglobin.
 
• Chlorophyll contains a porphyrin ring attached to a magnesium atom.
 
 
• An element that is also an important component of haemoglobin is known to be crucial during the synthesis of chlorophyll.
 
 
 
• For the synthesis of chlorophyll in plants, the elements needed are iron and magnesium.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Photosynthesis: The leaves have a green pigment called chlorophyll.

 
 
• It helps leaves capture the energy of the sunlight.
 
• This energy is used to synthesise food from carbon dioxide and water. 
 
• Since the synthesis of food occurs in the presence of sunlight, it is called photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• In the presence of sunlight Carbon dioxide + water + sunlight → Carbohydrate + oxygen.
 
• Some plants, green algae, and cyanobacteria can perform photosynthesis.
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts specifically, in the grana and stroma regions.
 
• The process of photosynthesis is commonly written as:

​

 underset{(Carbon dioxide)}{6CO₂} + underset{(Water)}{6H₂ O} xrightarrow[Chlorophyll]{Sunlight} underset{(Carbohydrates)}{C₆H₁₂O₆} + underset{(Oxygen)}{6O₂}

 
• The following events occur in plant cells during photosynthesis. 

 
 
• Absorption of light energy.
 
• Conversion of light energy into Chemical Energy.
 
• Storage of chemical energy in Sugars.
